# Pickbid

> A full-stack Next.js app for running amateur cricket leagues: design premium player cards, host real-time auctions spectators can watch live, track leaderboards and match results, and share everything with a single link — no app install required.

Key facts for working in this codebase:

- **Framework**: Next.js 16 (App Router, React 19, TypeScript). This is NOT older Next.js — APIs and conventions differ from common training data. Read the relevant guide in `node_modules/next/dist/docs/` before writing code, and heed deprecation notices.
- **Database**: PostgreSQL (Neon) accessed via Sequelize models (`src/lib/models.ts`); migrations via `sequelize-cli` in `migrations/`.
- **Auth**: NextAuth v5 (Auth.js), Google provider only. Player/upload APIs are intentionally anonymous — players create cards with a per-card `creatorToken`. Do NOT add session gating to player or upload routes.
- **Styling**: Tailwind CSS v4, shadcn/ui + Base UI, Motion, Lucide.
- **Media**: Cloudinary uploads. **Messaging**: WhatsApp Cloud API. **PDF**: jspdf + html2canvas-pro.
- **Hosting**: Vercel, deployed from the working tree via CLI (not git auto-deploy); env changes need a redeploy.
- **Commits**: Conventional Commits; releases automated by release-please.

## Documentation

- [README](README.md): Setup, environment variables, scripts, project structure, data model, deployment.
- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): Required reading rules for the Next.js 16 version in this repo.

Note: this file is the *codebase* map, for agents working in this repo. The
product-facing `llms.txt` served at `/llms.txt` — what Pickbid does, what it
costs, which public pages exist — is generated by
[src/app/llms.txt/route.ts](src/app/llms.txt/route.ts). Keep the two in step
when features change.

## Core source

- [Sequelize models & associations](src/lib/models.ts): users, leagues, teams, players, team_officials, matches, auction_live, user_badges, user_streaks.
- [Shared types](src/lib/types.ts): League, Player, Team, TeamOfficial, Match, LiveAuctionState, LivePurse.
- [Auth config](src/auth.ts): NextAuth Google setup; token.sub mapped to the DB user id.
- [Owner console auth](src/lib/adminAuth.ts): super-admin credentials read from `ADMIN_EMAIL`/`ADMIN_PASSWORD` env plus a signed HMAC session cookie. Deliberately separate from Auth.js — no admin row, flag, migration or seed, and a normal Google session never grants admin. The cookie name lives in [adminCookie.ts](src/lib/adminCookie.ts) so `proxy.ts` can read it without importing `next/headers`.
- [Database connection](src/lib/db.ts): Sequelize + pg, SSL required, pooled across hot reloads.
- [League workspace view](src/lib/leagueView.ts): `getLeagueView` — the signed-in league page's payload shaped for one viewer (roster trimming, organizer-only fields stripped). Shared by the server-rendered `/leagues/[id]` page and the league GET so the two can't disagree about what a viewer sees.
- [Landing showcase](src/lib/landingShowcase.ts): `getLandingShowcase` — the real cards, registration list, auction result and points table on the signed-out home page. Reads public leagues only, through `getPublicLeagueView`; one appearance per person, uploaded photos only, names cleaned of serial/phone numbers.
- [Card templates](src/lib/templates.ts): 12 colour templates for player cards.
- [Payment list PDFs](src/lib/paymentPdf.ts): the document register's Download menu — paid / unpaid lists, flat or team-wise (teams by name, teamless cards last, each team's paid count in its heading). Text-only jsPDF; names and receipt-on-file status, never the documents themselves.
- [League chrome](src/components/league/LeagueChrome.tsx): frames every `/leagues/[id]/*` screen with the navigation rail — an inset layout on desktop, where the page scrolls inside a rounded panel beside the rail, and a slide-over drawer under `lg` — and publishes `useLeagueRevision()` so a page reloads when the rail changes the league, plus `useLeagueScroller()` for scrolling the page (the panel on desktop, the window on a phone). [LeagueSidebar](src/components/league/LeagueSidebar.tsx) holds the links and the organizer actions; [leagueChrome.ts](src/lib/leagueChrome.ts) is the immersive-route matcher it shares with `NavBar`.
- [Badge catalog](src/lib/badges.ts): all 100 badges in six groups (career, auction, on the field, organizer, streaks, milestones) with their tiers and thresholds, plus the pure progress arithmetic. React-free and server-free, read by both sides. Badge ids are persisted in `user_badges` — never rename or reuse one.
- [Rewards evaluation](src/lib/rewards.ts): `checkInRewards` and `getRewardsOverview` — count the week towards the streak, read the user's metrics in one query, award new tiers. Lazy by design: badges are derived from existing tables on the user's own requests, never awarded from the write paths. The SQL is in the "Rewards" section of `store.ts`.
- [Rewards UI](src/components/rewards/): `BadgeMedal` (pure-CSS medal, see "Reward medals" in `globals.css`), the nav's `StreakChip` and throttled `RewardsWatcher`, the dashboard's `RewardsStrip`, the lazily loaded unlock toast, and `rewardsStore` — the client store they share. `requestRewardsCheck()` forces a check-in after an action likely to unlock something.
- [Fixture engine](src/lib/fixtures/index.ts): `generateFixtures` for every format (full round robin incl. home-and-away, matches per team, total matches, custom per-team min/max; rest and max-in-a-row rules; seeded shuffles), `validateFixture`, `scoreFixture` and `scheduleFixtures`. `plan.ts` turns a config into exact per-team targets and proves impossible ones impossible (parity, opponent counts, Erdős–Gallai); `select.ts` is a Havel–Hakimi backtracking search; `sequence.ts` orders matches into rounds. Pure, relative imports only — unit-tested by `npm test` (`fixtures.test.ts`). Shared by the public fixture tool, the matches screen's preview and the save endpoint; the form and preview UI are in [src/components/fixtures/](src/components/fixtures/FixtureOptions.tsx).
- [Fixture poster](src/lib/fixtures/poster.ts): thirteen templates in three moods — dark (Floodlight, Royal Gold, Crimson Strike, Midnight Neon, Platinum), light (Ivory Scorecard, Test Whites, Clean Sheet) and vibrant (Electric, Monsoon, Sunset Fest, Emerald Pitch, Jersey Blue), each a palette, a Google display face (with its measured `charWidth` for title fitting) and an ornament drawn in the renderer's `Ornaments` — three sizes (portrait, story, square), request validation and the pagination shared by the browser and the renderer. Rendered by `api/fixtures/poster`; the picker/preview dialog is [FixturePosterDialog](src/components/fixtures/FixturePosterDialog.tsx), on the public tool, the matches screen's generator preview and its saved Fixtures list.
- [Sold sound](src/lib/soldSound.ts): the watch screen's opt-in gavel-and-chime, synthesised with Web Audio (no asset). Browser-only; the context must be unlocked from a user gesture.
- [Certificate renderer](src/app/leagues/[id]/certificate/[playerId]/certificate.tsx): server-rendered participation certificate (satori), gated on the league's `certificatesReleasedAt`.
- [SEO config](src/lib/seo.ts): single source of truth for metadata, OG images, sitemap, robots.

## API routes (src/app/api)

- `auth/[...nextauth]`: NextAuth handlers.
- `leagues`: list (created/joined) and create leagues.
- `leagues/[id]`: get/update/delete a league with players, teams, officials. The GET body is `getLeagueView`, which the league page also renders from.
- `leagues/[id]/players`, `players/[playerId]`: player cards CRUD (anonymous via creatorToken). Contact numbers and payment receipts are blanked with `stripOrganizerFields` for anyone who can't manage the league.
- `leagues/[id]/teams`, `officials`, `matches`: team, official and match management. `matches/generate` saves a fixture previewed on the matches screen: the client posts the exact match list plus its config, the handler re-runs `validateFixture` against the league's current teams (so foreign or stale team ids are refused), derives rounds from the order, dates them if a schedule is given, and adds them alongside any existing matches.
- `leagues/[id]/auction/live`, `auction/live/summary`, `auction/reset`: live auction state broadcast/poll, the cheap "is an auction running right now" summary behind the LIVE banner, and reset.
- `leagues/[id]/ledger`: optional markdown income & expense sheet. Organizers read/write incl. drafts; league members read only once published; non-members 403 regardless of `isPublic`.
- `leagues/[id]/identity`: the organizer's document register — every player card with its entry-fee receipt (`players.paymentProofUrl`) and the ID document from the account it belongs to (`users.idProofUrl`). `requireLeagueManager` only, `private, no-store`, and no member-readable variant; neither document may reach a card, poster or PDF. `identity/[playerId]` PATCHes `players.paymentReceived` — the organizer's own confirmation that a fee arrived, on its own manager-gated endpoint precisely because the player PATCH also answers to a card's anonymous `creatorToken`.
- `leagues/[id]/can-manage`: just the caller's manage flag — the watch screen's cheap substitute for reading a whole league.
- `leagues/[id]/nav`: the scalars the league sidebar draws itself from — name, the three permission tiers, ledger/certificate state and two SQL-counted booleans. Same motive as `can-manage`: the rail renders on every league screen and must not pull the roster to decide which links to show.
- `leagues/[id]/clone`: duplicate a league.
- `profile/certificates`: participation certificates the signed-in user can download, scoped to their own player cards.
- `leagues/join`, `leagues/public`: join by code; public league directory.
- `fixtures/poster`: POST — one page of a fixture as a PNG poster (satori), PICKBID-watermarked. Anonymous and database-free: it renders only the teams and matches in the body, capped by `parsePosterInput`.
- `rewards/check-in`: POST — count this week towards the signed-in user's streak, award newly earned badge tiers, return the shell's summary (streak, unlocks, next goal). The `/rewards` page is server-rendered and evaluates on its own, with a `loading.tsx` so link prefetches never run that write.
- `profile`: user profile, including the optional identity proof (`idProofType` + `idProofUrl`) that leagues with `idProofRequired` check at self-registration. `upload`: Cloudinary image upload. `migrate`: admin-gated Redis→Postgres import.
- `admin/login`, `admin/logout`: owner console sign-in (env credentials, IP-throttled) and sign-out.
- `admin/overview`: whole-platform analytics, every league and every user in one payload. `admin/leagues/[id]`: owner overrides on any league — publish, open/close registration, release certificates, reset auction, clear the live broadcast, delete. Both gated by `requireAdmin`. An owner session additionally satisfies `requireLeagueManager` (but never `requireLeagueCreator`), so the owner can open any league's detail pages in full.

## Optional

- [Migrations](migrations/): Sequelize schema history.
- [Scripts](scripts/): favicon generation, Redis import, migration helpers.
- [Landing page](src/components/landing/Landing.tsx): the signed-out home page — a server component; the sign-in buttons ([SignInButton.tsx](src/components/landing/SignInButton.tsx)) are its only client island. Pictures in [visuals.tsx](src/components/landing/visuals.tsx) render the real `PlayerCard` with sample fallbacks; the serif display face is in [fonts.ts](src/components/landing/fonts.ts) and the `.landing-scope` theme at the end of `globals.css`.
